ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 4 — Sick Visit — Jesse Owens — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Same-day sick visit for a cold during chemoimmunotherapy

text.paragraph: Runny nose, sore throat and a dry cough for three days, twelve days after the second cycle. [S]

Mr. Owens called the oncology line on day 13 of his second cycle of nivolumab with carboplatin and pemetrexed and was seen the same day, as his warning list asks for any new cough. Three days ago he developed a runny nose and a scratchy throat, and since yesterday a dry cough, worst at night. Several children at a youth club where he spoke last week had colds. His highest temperature at home was 37.8 °C last night. He has no breathlessness: he walked his usual 3 km this morning, a little slower. He has no chest pain, no blood in his sputum, no diarrhea and no rash. He has not smoked since the first cycle and has had no urge to with the cough. He takes varenicline twice daily and had his dexamethasone only around the infusion. He is worried that the cough means the immunotherapy is affecting his lungs. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 1979-07-06; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Comfortable, talking in full sentences; temperature 37.6 °C
Oxygen saturation 96 percent at rest, as at his earlier visits, and 95 percent after a 6-minute corridor walk; respiratory rate 16
Head, eyes, ears, nose, and throat
Red throat without exudate; clear nasal discharge; no mouth ulcers
No tender or enlarged lymph nodes
Clear to auscultation throughout; no crackles or wheeze

Solid, spiculated 2.9 cm nodule in the left upper lobe with an enlarged (1.6 cm) left hilar lymph node on today's low-dose screening CT, Lung-RADS 4X (very suspicious); no symptoms of lung cancer. PET-CT, tissue diagnosis and thoracic oncology review booked
S — Synthetic presenting screening finding in a long-term smoker. Superseded by the diagnosis at the second visit.

Adenocarcinoma of the left upper lobe of the lung, cT1c N1 M0, stage IIB (AJCC 8th edition), resectable: 2.9 cm primary with a positive left interlobar (11L) node on EBUS; mediastinal nodes 4R, 4L and 7 negative; no metastases on PET-CT or brain MRI. PD-L1 tumor proportion score 40 percent (22C3); KRAS G12C mutation; no EGFR, ALK, ROS1, BRAF, MET exon 14, RET, NTRK or HER2 alteration
S — Synthetic histology, stage and biomarkers linked to his documented adenocarcinoma of the left lung; in the modern episode it is found by screening while still resectable.
Nicotine dependence, cigarettes: a pack a day for 35 years (35 pack-years); smokes his first cigarette within 30 minutes of waking; two attempts to stop, each lasting a few weeks without medicine
S — Synthetic modern entry linked to his documented smoking; superseded at the visit after surgery by nicotine dependence in early remission.

Acute viral upper respiratory infection (rhinovirus on a respiratory panel) on day 13 of cycle 2 of chemoimmunotherapy: runny nose, sore throat and a dry cough for three days, no hypoxia, clear chest X-ray; immune-related pneumonitis and pneumonia excluded; resolved
S — Synthetic intercurrent illness; not a historical claim.

value.displayName: Malignant neoplasm of upper lobe, left bronchus or lung

list.item:
Acute viral upper respiratory infection during chemoimmunotherapy (J06.9). A cold, with a respiratory panel positive for rhinovirus and negative for influenza, COVID-19 and RSV. A new cough on a checkpoint inhibitor must raise the question of immune-related pneumonitis; here the oxygen saturation is unchanged at rest and on walking, the lungs are clear and the chest X-ray shows no new opacity, so pneumonitis is not suspected and no steroid is needed. The neutrophil count is 3.2 and the temperature is low grade, so this is not a neutropenic fever and no antibiotic is needed. [S]
Rest, fluids, honey and saline nasal spray; acetaminophen for the sore throat if needed.
Call the 24-hour oncology line at once for a temperature of 38.0 °C or more, breathlessness, oxygen saturation below 94 percent on his home meter, chest pain, or a cough that keeps worsening after a week: that would need a CT of the chest for pneumonitis.
Cycle 3 as planned in nine days if he is recovering; the oncology team agreed.

Left upper lobe adenocarcinoma, stage IIB, on chemoimmunotherapy before surgery (C34.12). Two of three cycles given on schedule; the nodule looks smaller on today's X-ray. [S]
No change.

Nicotine dependence, on varenicline (F17.210). Still not smoking after nearly five weeks, even with the cough. [S]
Continue varenicline 1 mg twice daily.

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (2026); Schneider BJ, et al. Management of Immune-Related Adverse Events in Patients Treated With Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor Therapy: ASCO Guideline Update. J Clin Oncol 2021;39(36):4073-4126 (PMID 34724392) (2021)

Follow-up: Nurse telephone call in two days. Cycle 3 in nine days. Call the oncology line for any warning sign. Next scheduled visit 1979-08-05: after three cycles: restaging CT, decision for lobectomy, thyroid result and surgical preparation. [S]
